steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Good customer service creates competitive advantage: it builds loyalty, generates repeat business, and encourages positive word-of-mouth recommendations (free marketing).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Methods of delivering customer service: well-trained staff, clear returns policies, efficient complaint handling, after-sales support (warranties, helplines), personalised communication, and multichannel support (phone, email, chat, social media).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Monitoring customer service: customer feedback surveys, mystery shoppers, complaint analysis, online reviews, and Net Promoter Score (NPS).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Handling complaints effectively: listen, acknowledge, resolve quickly, and learn from the complaint to prevent recurrence. A well-handled complaint can increase customer loyalty.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two ways good customer service can benefit a business. | Describe how a business can monitor the quality of its customer service. | Evaluate whether investing in customer service training is more important than investing in marketing.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link customer service to financial outcomes: loyalty = repeat sales = revenue stability. When discussing complaints, remember: a well-handled complaint can actually IMPROVE customer loyalty (the 'service recovery paradox'). Use the 'cost of acquisition vs retention' statistic: it costs 5-7 times more to gain a new customer than keep an existing one.
